context_requirements: Cells must express soluble guanylyl cyclase (GUCY1A3/GUCY1B3) and have basal cGMP/PKG signaling to inhibit.
Endogenous NO/cGMP tone must be present; otherwise inhibition has little transcriptional effect.
Apoptosis-related transcriptional changes require a pro-apoptotic or stress context; healthy cells may show minimal response.
falsifiers: No consistent change in apoptosis-related landmark genes (e.g., BAD, BAX, CASP3, BCL2) at 24 h across cell lines.
Strong, reproducible upregulation of proliferation genes or downregulation of CDKN1A at 6 h, which would suggest a different mechanism.
Clear transcriptional response at 6 h in all nine lines, contradicting the expected slow/weak kinetics.
Lack of any dose-dependent or line-dependent differences, suggesting non-specific effects.

evidence.supports: sGC inhibitor ODQ increases caspase-3 activity, cytochrome c release, PARP cleavage, and DNA fragmentation, indicating cGMP mediates anti-apoptotic signaling.
sGC inhibitor ODQ increases apoptosis in pancreatic beta cells, showing that inhibition of cGMP signaling promotes cell death.
ODQ decreases PKG-mediated Bad phosphorylation and induces apoptosis in neural cells.
Methylene blue, described as a guanylyl cyclase inhibitor, prevents retinal damage and alters gene expression in a rat model.
